title: Create a queenside weakness
summary: Use the b-pawn against Black's queenside pawns, and use the a-file if it opens.
goal: Advance the b-pawn to challenge Black's queenside pawns and create targets.

steps.text: In the example, the a-pawn and b-pawn face three black queenside pawns. This pawn shape is called the Carlsbad structure.
In the example, the rook on b1 stands behind the b-pawn. Push the pawn to b4 when it is safe.
In the example, after a4 and b5, the b-pawn attacks c6. Check Black's reply before pushing.
If Black takes on b5 with the a-pawn and you retake with your a-pawn, the a-file opens. A rook can use it later; it is not an automatic win.

jobs.text: This rook stands behind your b-pawn.
The b-pawn can advance toward Black's queenside pawns.
The a-pawn can support the b-pawn after it reaches b5.

breaks.text: Advance the b-pawn to start the queenside plan.

opponent.text: Black can counter in the centre or on the kingside. Check threats before each pawn move.

notNow: Do not start a slow pawn advance while your king or a piece needs immediate defence.

mistakes.text: The immediate e4 push runs into a capture. Put the rook behind the b-pawn instead.

comments.text: Both a-pawns have left the a-file.
No black pawn can defend the c6 pawn.

exercises.prompt: White to move. Put a rook behind the b-pawn.

choices.why: The rook stands behind the b-pawn.
The immediate central push can be captured.

exercises.explanation: Rab1 supports the b-pawn's advance. Check the centre before pushing there.

exercises.prompt: White to move. Advance the b-pawn with the rook behind it.

choices.why: The central push gives Black a tactical opportunity.

exercises.explanation: b4 starts the queenside plan. The rook remains behind the pawn.

exercises.prompt: White to move. Attack the c6 pawn with the b-pawn.

choices.why: The b-pawn attacks c6 and a6.

exercises.explanation: b5 attacks two pawns. If Black takes with the a-pawn, your a-pawn can retake and open the a-file.
